name: Relevant Token Bucket and Redis Answer to Distributed Rate-Limiter
question: Design a distributed rate limiter that can handle 100,000 requests per second across multiple regions. How would you handle race conditions and synchronization?
candidate_answer: To design a distributed rate limiter for 100k RPS, I would use the Token Bucket algorithm backed by Redis as a centralized in-memory datastore. We maintain rate limits per user or API key, storing the current token count and timestamp of the last request. To prevent race conditions and concurrency conflicts, we use atomic operations in Redis so token inspection and decrement occur safely. If a client exceeds their limit, the service rejects the request with an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response code.
